lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is Tuesday's San Miguel County commissioners meeting, where four public hearings will take up proposed Land Use Code amendments that would add an entirely new Natural Resources article covering forestry, oil and gas, and geothermal operations — foundational rules that will govern extraction and resource use in this county for years. Alongside that, Telluride's HARC takes up the large-scale Shandoka redevelopment at 860 Black Bear Rd, the school board revisits the mill levy override discussion, and Norwood's Planning and Zoning digs into its own land use and master plan updates.

notable.stake: Land use and master plan updates will shape what gets built in Norwood.
First readings on 2027 water/sewer rates and Light Industrial zoning changes in Ouray.
First reading of Telluride Fire District's 2027 budget opens the public spending process.
Mill levy override funding discussion continues — school funding is on the line.
Public hearings on large Town-owned redevelopment at 860 Black Bear Rd.
Four public hearings on new county natural resource rules covering forestry, oil, and geothermal.
